citations.review_text:
I bought this game because I thought it was about jumping over squares.

A few minutes later I was arguing with a cube.

Then I found out people make levels harder than anything the developers ever imagined.

Then I watched someone beat one of those levels.

Now I understand why this game has been alive for so many years.

Simple idea.

Infinite skill ceiling.

Fantastic soundtrack.

My cube has exploded thousands of times.

It probably has thousands more left.

Recommended.

I got a game development degree just by staring at a menu screen.

10/10, currently crying after crashing at 99% on an easy demon.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the presence of a level editor and community-created levels.

citations.review_text:
Strongly Recommended – A Legendary Rhythm Platformer That Stands the Test of Time

Geometry Dash is one of the most unique and memorable platforming games ever created. It combines fast-paced gameplay, incredible music, challenging levels, and creative design into an experience that is simple to understand but difficult to master. Its easy controls make it accessible to everyone, while its demanding gameplay provides a satisfying challenge for players who want to improve.

The game's biggest strength is the feeling of progression. Every attempt helps players improve their timing, reaction speed, and consistency. Completing difficult levels feels extremely rewarding, and the journey from struggling with a level to finally beating it creates some of the most satisfying moments in gaming.

Another major feature that makes Geometry Dash special is its community and level editor. Players have created millions of unique levels with creative designs, unique gameplay ideas, and impressive visuals. This endless amount of community-made content gives the game incredible replay value and ensures there is always something new to experience.

The soundtrack and visual style are also major highlights. Each song perfectly matches the gameplay, making every jump and movement feel connected to the music. The colorful graphics, smooth effects, and creative decorations give Geometry Dash a style that remains recognizable and enjoyable even after many years.

For anyone who enjoys challenging gameplay, great music, and endless creativity, Geometry Dash is an easy recommendation. It is a true classic that continues to entertain players years after release and remains one of the best rhythm-based platformers ever made.

This is hands-down the best game I've ever played. It might seem dull and boring and just a copy of the Impossible Game but this block jumping over a spike game has literally changed my life. The creating menu is literally a game engine (Not joking). You can get custom blocks if you want. There's even LORE to this game. The rush you feel when you beat a new hardest level or die at 58% (we don't talk about that) is UNMATCHED. Plus, even if it gets stale? GEODE. If you don't know what Geode is, it's a mod loader in Geometry Dash. And it makes the game HUNDREDS of times more fun to play. If you ever get the chance, please play this game.

citations.review_text: This game is highly addictive and entertaining despite having a one-button gameplay loop. Pooping yourself while trying to clear Electrodynamix is basically a rite of passage. Fun gameplay and user generated content.

At first glance, this game appears to be the epitome or simplicity: a tiny cube, a single button, and an obstacle course seemingly designed by someone with an unhealthy obsession with triangles. One might reasonably assume that such a minimalist concept would provide a relaxing pastime.

What begins as an innocent exercise in rhythm soon escalates into a prolonged negotiation with your own sanity. The game possesses an extraordinary talent for convincing you that victory is perpetually one attempt away a proposition it has successfully marketed to millions of players who have now spent several thousand attempts proving precisely the opposite.

The soundtrack is nothing short of phenomenal. Each level is choreographed with such impeccable precision that you'll eventually find yourself humming the music in the shower, involuntarily associating every beat drop with a traumatic memory of exploding at 97%

Then there's the community a gathering of individuals who have apparently transcended conventional human limitations. While the average player celebrates surviving for thirty seconds. someone else casually uploads a video entitled "Extreme Demon Completed Blindfolded Using a Banana as a Controller (First Attempt)." :D Naturally, the comments complain that the level was too easy.

Yet somehow, despite the repeated humiliation, shattered confidence, and occasional existential crisis triggered by a fluorescent cube, you always return. There is an irresistible satisfaction in finally conquering a level that spent the previous week treating your self-esteem like a disposable resource.

10/10. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who has recently experienced far too much happiness and wishes to restore balance to the universe. :D

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as rhythm-based and built around controlling a character with a single button.

citations.review_text:
Geometry Dash is a rich evolution of the old, nostalgic Impossible Game :
A rythm-based game built on a simple gameplay principle : using only 1 button to control and complete levels.

GD is a rich exploration of all the possibilities allowed by this gameplay concept.
Moreover, last updates introduced revolutionary changes in both graphics and level dynamics, allowing users to create and introduce their own levels. 

Difficulty spans from super easy to extremely difficult, fitting everyone's level (whether you be an untalented human or an alien with superhuman reflexes)

An inexpensive game with a rich and surprising world...

This is a game where the whole premise is clicking one button to jump over spikes. Despite this, this game is a test of timing, precision and nerve control. This and multiple other factors makes this one of the hardest games ever created, with new ways to push yourself always appearing. I would definitely recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the extensive content available through user-created levels and the level editor.

citations.review_text:
Undeniably my favorite game of all time, and the longest game I have ever played. Been goin at it since November 2014 on my iPhone, and because I played on another Steam account before this isn't even my accurate number of hours in this game.
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
I don't want to get too deep into this because the gameplay of GD can get very complex. But it's one that can be repetitive, but is also insanely addicting. It is quite hard to master, and it's not like I am even perfect at this game, far from it. But because of the vast skill ceiling of jumping over spikes, flying, and many more gamemodes, it feels like you never run out of things to do in this game. Not only from mastering the main levels, but also playing through thousands and millions of custom-made levels, a good chunk of which are high quality. Plus with both classic, the standard auto-scroller, and platformer modes, it really does feel like there's plenty to do and to get really into. There also is the editor, but I'm more of a player than a creator. To put simply, the editor in here is very powerful(but also quite tough to fully learn).
[h2]Performance & Polish[/h2]
This is a very simple game graphics wise, and can run on basically anything(even a smart fridge I've seen). The game also features a low detail mode, whether for the entire game, or it can be enabled per custom level as some creators get very detailed in their levels. Because of the game's physics and how that all works, there are other performance options too you can use to ensure gameplay feels smooth to play. It is worth noting I use the popular mod manager Geode for this game, and have gotten performance mods and the Megahack overlay to help with my experience. Vanilla GD still offers a good amount of options, but I'd recommend getting Geode/Megahack if you want a more full experience.
[h2]Value[/h2]
Like I said, because the gameplay is so addicting it feels like you never run out of things to do. I keep forgetting this game is only $5 …
